crossRefs.note: Every wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
She opens her mouth with wisdom. Kind instruction is on her tongue.
Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears Yahweh, she shall be praised.
Give her of the fruit of her hands! Let her works praise her in the gates!
Nabal answered David’s servants, and said, “Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse? There are many servants who break…
Shall I then take my bread, my water, and my meat that I have killed for my shearers, and give it to men who I don’t…
Now therefore know and consider what you will do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his house…
For the wicked boasts of his heart’s cravings. He blesses the greedy and condemns Yahweh.
The fool will no longer be called noble, nor the scoundrel be highly respected.

people.name: Abigail
people.line: Wife of Nabal, later married David

people.name: Caleb
people.line: Faithful spy, given Hebron as inheritance

people.name: Nabal
people.line: Wealthy Carmelite; husband of Abigail. He was known for foolishness.

translations.web: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail. This woman was intelligent and had a beautiful face; but the man was surly and evil in his doings. He was of the house of Caleb.
translations.bsb: His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.
translations.kjv: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.
translations.asv: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail; and the woman was of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.
